subject: Dedicated capacity — sizing contingency & temporary reservation for AstroEdge POC
messages:
From: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@astroedge.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask for POC (throughput + latency targets)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed. We're moving into a short POC to validate inference quality and latency for our edge analytics product. High level:
- Traffic profile: 1,200 req/s average, peaks to ~2,400 req/s (short bursts)
- Typical prompt length: 40–90 tokens, avg ~65 tokens
- Latency target: p95 < 250 ms, p99 ideally < 400 ms
- Model: we want to use rwdx-large-v1 (licensed) with KV caching enabled
- Duration: initial POC 45 days, then a phased production rollout if all good

Can you confirm if Redwood can hold dedicated capacity for us during the POC window, and give a ballpark on GPU count (we're flexible on exact SKU but prefer a sensible cost/latency tradeoff)? Also would need quick SOC2/compliance checklist for procurement.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Shaw
Head of Platform
AstroEdge
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@astroedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for POC (throughput + latency targets)

Ethan —

Appreciate the details, that helps a lot. Quick clarifying Qs before our sizing:
1) Concurrency vs QPS: is 1,200 req/s your sustained QPS or concurrency target (do you expect many long-lived streaming sessions)?
2) Token distribution: are there any long-tail requests beyond 500 tokens we should account for?
3) Traffic shape: do spikes to 2,400 last seconds, minutes, or longer?

PreliminaRy sizing notes (ballpark):
- With rwdx-large-v1 and KV cache enabled, and assuming quantized execution (int8) and continuous batching, we estimate roughly 10–14 A100-80GB equivalent GPUs to maintain p95 < 250ms at ~1,200 sustained req/s (~65 tokens avg). If you plan for sudden bursts to 2,400 req/s for multiple minutes, add a 30–50% buffer (so ~14–21 GPUs).
- If you prefer a lower-cost SKU (A10/A6000-class), expect ~1.6–2x the count depending on batch/quantization choices.
- Caching (prefix & KV) will reduce per-request work significantly for repeat contexts; we should understand reuse ratio.

Markus — can you validate the quick GPU math and operational constraints?

Next steps: I'll pull together a capacity worksheet and a provisional hold proposal (30 days) while we surface SOC2 artifacts for Nina/Procurement.

—So
So­ojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for POC (throughput + latency targets)

So- —

Validated Soojin's ballpark with infra sim and recent perf runs:
- Baseline assumptions: rwdx-large-v1, int8 quant, avg 65 tokens, batching latency target 25–40ms per batch; effective throughput per A100-80GB ~8k tokens/sec under these conditions.
- Tokens/sec estimate: 1,200 req/s * 65 tokens = 78k tokens/sec sustained. That maps to ~10 GPUs (78k / 8k = 9.75).
- Add 30% headroom for bursty traffic + ops margin -> 13 GPUs. If AstroEdge wants p99 < 400ms with multi-minute spikes to 2,400 req/s, plan for 18–20 GPUs.
- Operational notes: KV cache hit-rate assumption critical. If hit-rate < 20% we should re-evaluate (more compute). Also consider enabling response streaming which slightly increases CPU/network pressure on the front-end nodes; planning includes those nodes but not in the GPU count above.

We can hold a provisional pool: request a 30-day soft reservation on ~15 A100-equivalent slots (label: AE-POC-APR27). This will be reversible but will reduce our ability to reassign those cards for other short-term bursts. To proceed I need a ticket from sales to Infra (JIRA-INFRA-1427) with the following: start/end dates, target SKU (A100-80GB or A10), and expected SLA bump (if any).

I'll attach a quick capacity worksheet I used for the calc.

—Markus
Director, Serving Infra
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for POC (throughput + latency targets) — provisional reservation

Ethan/Nina —

Following up with a short summary and proposed next steps:
- Preliminary sizing: 13 GPUs (A100-equivalent) with a recommended contingency plan up to 18–20 GPUs if you expect multi-minute bursts to 2,400 req/s.
- Proposal: Redwood can place a provisional 30-day soft reservation of 15 A100-equivalent slots to cover the POC. This prevents reallocation but is reversible if timelines shift.
- Attachments: capacity_worksheet_astroedge.xlsx (detailed assumptions) and SLA_Draft_AstroEdge.pdf (standard 30/60/90 day terms).

Action items:
1) AstroEdge: confirm preferred SKU (A100 vs A10-class), expected burst duration, and whether you want streaming enabled.
2) Procurement: please review the SLA draft and confirm SOC2 needs (we will provide SOC2 Type II package link).
3) Redwood sales: Marissa, can you open the JIRA-INFRA-1427 ticket and enter the AE-POC-APR27 reservation? Markus will then attach a soft hold.

If you want, we can lock the reservation upon receipt of a signed MSA or a non-binding LOI + PO. Otherwise we'll hold for 30 days from the reservation start date.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the worksheet.

Best,
So­ojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
